engine.note: No hosted Supabase project, production system, or third-party system was contacted.

steps.note: The handler cannot complete its work. What it leaves behind is the whole question.
steps.label: Attempt 1 — the downstream dependency is unavailable
steps.detail: The commitment failed (downstream payment ledger unavailable) but the error was swallowed and logical event evt_hl0817_settled remains marked processed, so no retry will ever be accepted.

steps.note: The same delivery id, retried. A receiver that recorded attempt 1 as processed will discard this.
steps.label: Attempt 2 — the provider retries the same delivery
steps.detail: The ledger already held delivery id del_hl0817_flaky, so this attempt was discarded — including when it was the provider retrying work that never completed.

vulnerable.title: Processing fails downstream, and the provider retries the same delivery
vulnerable.intent: The dependency the handler writes to is unavailable on the first attempt. The provider retries the same delivery id, as an at-least-once provider does, and the dependency is available by then.
vulnerable.consequence: If the event was marked processed before the work was done, the retry is discarded as a duplicate and the payment is lost silently — no error, no queue, no alert, and a customer who paid.
vulnerable.expectation_text: The failed attempt leaves nothing behind, and the retry produces exactly one commitment of 91200 cents.

steps.note: The outage begins.
steps.label: Attempt 1 — dependency unavailable
steps.detail: The commitment failed (downstream payment ledger unavailable) but the error was swallowed and logical event evt_nw2042_settled remains marked processed, so no retry will ever be accepted.

steps.note: The provider backs off and retries.
steps.label: Attempt 2 — dependency still unavailable
steps.detail: The ledger already held delivery id del_nw2042_outage, so this attempt was discarded — including when it was the provider retrying work that never completed.

steps.note: The outage continues past the point where a fragile receiver has already given up.
steps.label: Attempt 3 — dependency still unavailable
steps.detail: The ledger already held delivery id del_nw2042_outage, so this attempt was discarded — including when it was the provider retrying work that never completed.

steps.note: Recovery. Whether this attempt can still commit is what separates a recoverable receiver from a lossy one.
steps.label: Attempt 4 — the dependency is restored
steps.detail: The ledger already held delivery id del_nw2042_outage, so this attempt was discarded — including when it was the provider retrying work that never completed.

vulnerable.title: A sustained outage across three attempts, then recovery
vulnerable.intent: The dependency stays unavailable for three consecutive delivery attempts and is restored before the fourth. This is the shape of a real incident rather than a single blip.
vulnerable.consequence: A receiver that cannot survive a multi-attempt outage loses every event that arrived during it, and the loss is only discovered by reconciliation, if at all.
vulnerable.expectation_text: Three failed attempts change nothing, and the attempt after recovery produces exactly one commitment of 32500 cents.

steps.note: The failure that prompts the incident.
steps.label: Attempt 1 — dependency unavailable
steps.detail: The commitment failed (downstream payment ledger unavailable) but the error was swallowed and logical event evt_hl0818_settled remains marked processed, so no retry will ever be accepted.

steps.note: Automatic recovery completes.
steps.label: Attempt 2 — the provider retries and succeeds
steps.detail: The ledger already held delivery id del_hl0818_flaky, so this attempt was discarded — including when it was the provider retrying work that never completed.

steps.note: The same logical event under a new delivery id, sent by hand after the incident.
steps.label: An operator also replays the event from the dashboard
steps.detail: Delivery del_hl0818_replay was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 15000 cents was made for HL-0818.

vulnerable.title: Recovery followed by a manual replay must not double-apply
vulnerable.intent: After a failure and a successful retry, an operator also replays the same logical event from the provider dashboard — the ordinary human response to an incident, and the point at which a fragile receiver turns one incident into two.
vulnerable.consequence: Recovery work itself becomes the cause of the duplicate commitment, which is the failure mode operators are least likely to anticipate.
vulnerable.expectation_text: Recovery and the manual replay together still leave exactly one commitment of 15000 cents.

steps.note: The outage affects this delivery only.
steps.label: An unrelated delivery fails
steps.detail: The commitment failed (downstream payment ledger unavailable) but the error was swallowed and logical event evt_nw2042_settled remains marked processed, so no retry will ever be accepted.

steps.note: It must be processed normally.
steps.label: The unrelated event for NW-2041 is delivered
steps.detail: Delivery del_nw2041_c was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 148000 cents was made for NW-2041.

steps.note: The failure continues around the healthy event.
steps.label: The failing delivery is retried and fails again
steps.detail: The ledger already held delivery id del_nw2042_outage, so this attempt was discarded — including when it was the provider retrying work that never completed.

vulnerable.title: An unrelated event delivered during the outage window
vulnerable.intent: While one delivery is failing repeatedly, an unrelated invoice.paid event for a different invoice arrives and must be processed normally.
vulnerable.consequence: If a single failing dependency stalls unrelated events, an isolated outage becomes a total processing outage.
vulnerable.expectation_text: The unrelated event commits exactly once, in both documented configurations, regardless of the failure around it.

steps.note: The provider's first delivery of the logical event. Nothing has been processed yet.
steps.label: First delivery of evt_nw2041_paid
steps.detail: Delivery del_nw2041_a was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 148000 cents was made for NW-2041.

steps.note: A second delivery carrying the SAME event_id under a different delivery_id. A receiver keyed on the delivery id sees something it has never seen before.
steps.label: Replay: same logical event, new delivery id
steps.detail: Delivery del_nw2041_b was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 148000 cents was made for NW-2041.

vulnerable.title: The same logical event is delivered twice
vulnerable.intent: The provider delivers invoice.paid for NW-2041, then delivers the same logical event again under a new delivery id — an at-least-once redelivery, a dashboard replay, or a backfill all look like this.
vulnerable.consequence: The customer is committed twice for one payment. Duplicate charges, duplicated fulfilment, and a revenue figure that no longer matches the provider's are the ordinary results.
vulnerable.expectation_text: One commitment of 148000 cents for NW-2041, no matter how many times the event arrives.

steps.note: The payload is well formed and the endpoint is correct; only the signature fails to recompute.
steps.label: Forged delivery with an unverifiable signature
steps.detail: Delivery del_nw2042_forged was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 32500 cents was made for NW-2042.

vulnerable.title: A forged event with a signature that does not verify
vulnerable.intent: A caller posts a well-formed invoice.paid body to the endpoint carrying a signature that does not recompute from the payload.
vulnerable.consequence: Anyone who learns the endpoint URL can mark invoices paid, extend subscriptions, or release fulfilment without paying.
vulnerable.expectation_text: No commitment at all, because the body was not proven to come from the provider.

steps.note: The newer version of the invoice arrives and is applied.
steps.label: Current event: sequence 2, 15000 cents
steps.detail: Delivery del_hl0818_v2 was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 15000 cents was made for HL-0818.

steps.note: The older version of the same invoice arrives after the newer one. It is correctly signed and is not a duplicate — only its order is wrong.
steps.label: Superseded event: sequence 1, 9000 cents, arriving late
steps.detail: Delivery del_hl0818_v1 was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 9000 cents was made for HL-0818.

vulnerable.title: A superseded event arrives after the newer one
vulnerable.intent: Sequence 2 of HL-0818 is delivered first and applied. Sequence 1, the older version of the same invoice, then arrives late — the ordinary result of a provider retry racing a fresh delivery.
vulnerable.consequence: A stale amount overwrites the current one, so the recorded balance silently disagrees with the provider's.
vulnerable.expectation_text: Only the newer sequence 2 event is applied; the superseded sequence 1 event changes nothing.

steps.note: The ordinary, legitimate case.
steps.label: Single correctly signed first delivery
steps.detail: Delivery del_hl0817_clean was recorded in the ledger and one commitment of 91200 cents was made for HL-0817.

vulnerable.title: A legitimate, correctly signed, first-time event
vulnerable.intent: A single properly signed invoice.paid event for HL-0817 that has never been seen before. This is the path that must keep working after the fix.
vulnerable.consequence: If this path stops committing, the remediation has broken payment processing rather than secured it.
vulnerable.expectation_text: Exactly one commitment of 91200 cents, in both documented configurations.
